items.quote: generate a user token from your Brex dashboard and pass it along in your API call headers.
items.why: Supports bearer token part only; says nothing about oauth2 or the admin-creates-token detail.

items.quote: For all other APIs, you will implement the Authorization Code Grant
items.why: Shows Authorization Code Grant for other APIs, i.e. oauth2 exists; the rest of the claim is not covered.

items.quote: If you are using the onboarding API, you will generate a Client Credentials Grant as there is no existing Brex client involved.
items.why: Supports Client Credentials use for onboarding API only; does not cover the full auth method list.

items.quote: This guide assumes you are a Brex customer with admin access to your dashboard.
items.why: Assumes a customer with admin access; related to customer_account gate but not stating it is required or the agreement part.

items.quote: to be issued a client ID and client secret for partner authentication.
items.why: Says partner client ID and secret are issued; does not say they come from developer support or name the multi-tenant gate.

items.quote: The team API lets you manage users, departments, locations, and cards.
items.why: Team API manages users, departments, locations, cards; covers part of listed scope, not REST/OpenAPI or other APIs.

items.quote: The server is hosted at `https://api.brex.com/mcp` and supports any MCP-compatible client.
items.why: States server hosted at the exact URL and is MCP-compatible; vendor-official is implied by the vendor's own hosting, not stated.

items.quote: MCP clients that support OAuth will automatically initiate a browser-based authorization flow when you first connect.
items.why: Describes OAuth browser flow for MCP clients; implies a server exists but does not establish existence or official status.
